newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCC rates ease off peak, Suezmaxes soften.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCC rates ease off peak, Suezmaxes soften.

text.p: The key Middle East tanker market for very large crude carriers (VLCCs) looked to have peaked by the middle of this week and was starting to head lower on Friday, shipping brokers said.
Activity remained slightly below normal levels but despite a slight softening, larger VLCCs were still commanding healthy rates.
"Large VLCCs are looking at close to W60 for a trip West and even a 350,000 tonner can expect W55 for US Gulf and W57.5 for northwest Europe," said brokers Galbraith's Ltd.
Rates for eastern routes from the Gulf were also slipping, with CPC fixing the Saudi Splendour to take 247,000 tonnes to Taiwan at W70.5 loading June 26, down a couple of points.
Exxon also managed to fix a VLCC at W70 for a trip to Singapore.
"Modern ships are still looking at higher numbers... but the signs are now pointing slightly downwards," Galbraith's said.

Spot market volumes in the Aframax or 130,000-tonne sector also remained relatively depressed, particularly in West Africa which again saw a lower than average number of fixings and rates were marked down five points to W90 for a transatlantic trip.
Rates in the Mediterranean for the same sized vessels were broadly steady to a shade softer at W92.50.

Aframax vessels were commanding similar rates for trips within northwest Europe, but the trend was upwards, with inter-UK/Continent trade heading towards W100 and cross-Med routes towards W110, brokers said.
